gloss: hand; give thanks, acknowledge, confess; throw
summary: יָד is the hand, and with it what a hand holds and does: power and possession (“given into your hand”), the one through whom a thing is done (“by the hand of Moses”, Num 10:13), a side or place, a share, a monument (2Sa 18:18), and Yahweh’s own hand, his power at work (Deu 26:8; Ezk 37:1). The verb יָדָה in its qal and piel is to throw or cast (Jer 50:14; Lam 3:53); its hiphil, nearly all its uses, is to acknowledge openly: to give thanks to Yahweh for what he is and does (Psa 136:1) and to confess one’s sin to him (Psa 32:5), and its hithpael is confession of sin, as over the goat of the day of covering (Lev 16:21). תּוֹדָה is that thanksgiving, the thank offering, and confession. Whether the verb comes from the hand is not shown: הוֹדָה and הִתְוַדָּה keep a w, as Ge'ez wadaya “throw” and Aramaic and Syriac ʾawdī “give thanks” do, while the hand is yad in every language, so the noun and the verb may be two older roots in one spelling.

words.gloss: hand; power, control; agency (“by the hand of”); side; share; monument
words.summary: About 1,600 uses. The hand itself; then what is in a man’s hand, his power and possession; the hand through which another acts; and by likeness a side, a share, a pillar, the tenons and arms of things. The noun has no verb of its own in Hebrew; the verb יָדָה in this entry may belong to another older root (see the root’s summary).

senses.definition: The hand, or the arm with it: what a man reaches out with, takes, holds, lifts and lays on a thing.

evidence.note: “Lest he put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life.”
“The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau”: the hands felt for their hair.
When Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed; Aaron and Hur held up his hands until sunset.
Aaron lays his two hands on the head of the living goat.
“Without you no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
“When you spread out your hands … your hands are full of blood.”

senses.definition: What is “in the hand” of someone is in his power or keeping; to give into a hand is to hand over to his control, to deliver from a hand is to free from it.

evidence.note: Every beast and fish: “into your hand they are given.”
Abram to Sarai: “Your maid is in your hand; do to her what is good in your eyes.”
Yahweh gave them into the hand of plunderers and sold them into the hand of their enemies.
Blessed be Yahweh, who delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharaoh.
“I kill and I make alive … and there is none who delivers out of my hand.”
“My times are in your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies.”
“Into your hand I commit my spirit”, quoted by Jesus on the cross (Luk 23:46).
“In his hand are the depths of the earth.”
“My strength and the might of my hand have made me this wealth.”
“Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength.”

senses.gloss: the hand of Yahweh: his power at work
senses.definition: Yahweh’s hand is his power put forth: in delivering Israel and striking Egypt, in creation, and on a prophet, moving him to see and to speak.

evidence.note: “Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm.”
“The hand of Yahweh is on your cattle in the field”: the plague.
“With a strong hand Yahweh brought you out of Egypt.”
“Is the hand of Yahweh shortened?”: is his power too small to do it?
“The hand of Yahweh is not shortened, that it cannot save.”
“All these things my hand made”, quoted by Stephen (Act 7:50).
The word of Yahweh came to Ezekiel “and the hand of Yahweh was on him there”.
“The spirit lifted me up … and the hand of Yahweh was strong on me.”
“The hand of Yahweh was on me, and he brought me out by the spirit of Yahweh”: hand and spirit side by side.
When the minstrel played, “the hand of Yahweh came on him” and Elisha prophesied.
“Let us fall into the hand of Yahweh, for his mercies are many, but let me not fall into the hand of man.”

senses.gloss: by the hand of: through, by means of
senses.definition: בְּיַד with a person names the one through whom another acts or speaks: Yahweh commands by the hand of Moses, sends his word by the hand of the prophets.

evidence.note: They set out the first time “at the mouth of Yahweh by the hand of Moses”: Yahweh commands, Moses passes it on.
Aaron and his sons did all that Yahweh commanded by the hand of Moses.
The statutes Yahweh gave on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
The commandments Yahweh commanded by the hand of Moses in the plains of Moab.
Yahweh warned Israel “by the hand of all his prophets”.
The word of Yahweh came by the hand of Haggai the prophet.
The burden of the word of Yahweh to Israel by the hand of Malachi.

senses.definition: What a man’s hand “reaches” or “finds” is what he can afford; the law fits the offering and the valuation to it.

evidence.note: “If his hand cannot reach to a lamb”, two turtledoves or two young pigeons.
Two turtledoves or two young pigeons, “such as his hand can reach”.
“If his hand has not found enough to give back to him”, the land stays with the buyer until the jubilee.
The priest values the poor man “according to what the hand of the vower can reach”.

senses.definition: By likeness, the side of a thing or the place beside it: the bank of a river, the side of a road, a man’s own place in the camp or on the wall.

evidence.note: The Canaanite dwells by the sea and “on the hand of the Jordan”: along its side.
Pharaoh’s daughter’s maids walked “on the hand of the river”.
“All the hand of the river Jabbok”: its whole side.
Eli sat on a seat “by the hand of the road”, watching.
The tribes set out “each in his place (עַל־יָדוֹ)” by their standards.
“And at his hand (next to him) built the men of Jericho.”

senses.definition: A portion counted out, and so, with a number, so many times over.

evidence.note: Benjamin’s portion was “five hands” more than any of theirs.
A fifth to Pharaoh, “and four hands (parts) shall be yours” for seed and food.
The king found them “ten hands”, ten times, better than all the magicians.
Israel to Judah: “We have ten hands in the king.”

senses.definition: A pillar set up to keep a name in memory, called a hand.

evidence.note: Saul came to Carmel “and behold, he set up a hand for himself”.
Absalom set up a pillar, “for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance; … it is called the hand of Absalom to this day.”
To the eunuchs who keep his covenant Yahweh gives “in my house and within my walls יָד וָשֵׁם, a hand and a name, better than sons and daughters”.

senses.definition: The parts of a made thing that stick out or hold, as a hand does: the tenons of the tabernacle’s boards, the axles of the stands, the arms of a throne.

evidence.note: “Two hands for each board, joined one to another”: tenons.
“The hands of the wheels were in the stand”: axles.
Solomon’s throne had “hands on either side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the hands”: arm-rests.

evidence.locator: Psa.31.6, בְּיָדְךָ → χεῖράς; Psa.102.26, יָדֶיךָ → χειρῶν; Isa.65.2, יָדַי → χεῖράς; Jer.31.32, בְיָדָם → χειρὸς; χείρ renders יָד ×1239

evidence.note: “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit”: Psa 31:6.
“The heavens are the works of your hands”: Psa 102:26.
“All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient people”: Isa 65:2.
“In the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt”: Jer 31:32.
“Did not my hand make all these things?”: Isa 66:2.
“A fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God”; compare 2Sa 24:14.

parallels.note: “Arm”: a strong hand and an outstretched arm.
The spirit of Yahweh beside his hand on the prophet.
Hand and foot together: any movement at all.

phrases.gloss: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
give into the hand of: hand over to
fill the hand: consecrate to priestly service

evidence.note: “Anoint them and fill their hand and sanctify them, that they may serve me as priests.”
“Now you have filled your hand to Yahweh”: of the whole assembly.
“The land which I lifted my hand to give to Abraham.”
“I lift my hand to heaven and say, As I live forever.”

phrases.gloss: lean the hand on: lay a hand on an offering or a man

evidence.note: He lays his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it is accepted for him to cover him.
Moses lays his hands on Joshua.

phrases.gloss: with a high hand: openly, defiantly

evidence.note: Israel went out of Egypt “with a high hand in the eyes of all the Egyptians”.
The soul who sins “with a high hand” blasphemes Yahweh and is cut off: presumptuous sin, against the unwitting sin of 15:27–29.

phrases.gloss: a strong hand and an outstretched arm
a hand and a name: a lasting memorial

words.gloss: throw, cast; (hiphil) give thanks, praise, acknowledge, confess; (hithpael) confess
words.summary: 114 uses, 100 of them hiphil. The qal and piel, three uses in all, are to throw or cast; the hiphil and hithpael are to acknowledge openly, in thanks to Yahweh or in confession of sin. Scripture does not show how the two meanings join, nor whether either comes from יָד, the hand.

evidence.locator: Psa.18.50, אוֹדְךָ → ἐξομολογήσομαί; Psa.136.1, הוֹדוּ → ἐξομολογεῖσθε; Dan.9.4, וָאֶתְוַדֶּה → ἐξωμολογησάμην; ἐξομολογέω and its forms render יָדָה about 80 times

evidence.note: “Therefore I will ἐξομολογήσομαί you among the nations and sing to your name”: Psa 18:50, אוֹדְךָ בַגּוֹיִם.
Baptised by John “ἐξομολογούμενοι their sins”, as Israel confessed theirs (Neh 9:2).
“I ἐξομολογοῦμαί you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth.”
“Confess your faults one to another.”

senses.definition: Let fly at a target: shoot arrows at an enemy.

evidence.note: “All you who bend the bow, shoot (יְדוּ) at her; spare no arrow.”

senses.definition: Throw a thing at or down: stones at a man, the horns of the nations down to the ground.

evidence.note: “They cut off my life in the pit and cast (וַיַּדּוּ) a stone on me.”
The craftsmen come “to cast down (לְיַדּוֹת) the horns of the nations” that scattered Judah.

senses.definition: Declare openly, before others, what Yahweh is and has done: thank him for his goodness and faithfulness. It stands beside “sing praise” and “bless”, and its fixed refrain gives its reason: “for he is good, for his חֶסֶד is forever”.

evidence.note: “Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his חֶסֶד is forever”, the refrain of the whole psalm (136:2–3, 26).
Leah at Judah’s birth: “This time I will praise (אוֹדֶה) Yahweh.”
“I will give thanks to you among the nations and sing praise to your name”, quoted in Rom 15:9.
“It is good to give thanks to Yahweh and to sing praises to your name, Most High.”
“Enter his gates with תּוֹדָה …; give thanks to him, bless his name.”
“Let them thank Yahweh for his חֶסֶד and his wonders to the sons of man”, four times (107:15, 21, 31).
“All your works shall thank you, and your faithful ones bless you.”
“I will thank you, Yahweh; though you were angry with me, your anger turned away and you comforted me.”
“The living, the living, he thanks you, as I do this day”, against the grave and death that cannot (38:18).
The singers “to praise and to give thanks to Yahweh”, and the house was filled with a cloud.
At the founding of the second house they sang “praising and giving thanks to Yahweh, for he is good”.
In restored Jerusalem, the voice of those saying “Give thanks to Yahweh of hosts”.
Jeduthun prophesied with the harp “to give thanks and to praise Yahweh”.
The tribes go up “to give thanks to the name of Yahweh”.

senses.definition: Own openly to Yahweh what one has done, the opposite of covering it.

evidence.note: “My iniquity I did not cover; I said, I will confess (אוֹדֶה) my transgressions to Yahweh, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.”
“He who covers his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses (מוֹדֶה) and forsakes them will find mercy.”
If Israel is struck down for its sin and turns again “and confesses your name” and prays in this house.

senses.definition: Of men toward a man: praise him, or own what he is or can do.

evidence.note: “Judah, you, your brothers shall praise you (יוֹדוּךָ)”: the name heard again.
“Men praise you when you do well for yourself.”
Of the king: “the peoples shall praise you forever and ever”.
Yahweh to Job: “Then I too will acknowledge to you that your own right hand can save you.”

senses.definition: Speak out one’s own or one’s people’s sin before Yahweh: required of the guilty with his offering or restitution, done by the high priest over the living goat, and by Daniel, Ezra and Nehemiah for the nation.

evidence.note: “When he is guilty in one of these, he shall confess that in which he sinned”, and then bring his guilt offering.
Aaron lays his hands on the living goat “and confesses over it all the iniquities of the sons of Israel”, putting them on its head.
“They shall confess their sin that they have done” and restore it in full with a fifth added.
“If they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers … then I will remember my covenant with Jacob” (26:40–42).
“I prayed to Yahweh my God and confessed.”
Ezra praying and confessing, weeping and casting himself down before the house of God.
Israel stood “and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers”.

senses.definition: Once of thanks: the Levites at Hezekiah’s feast “giving thanks to Yahweh”.

evidence.note: Seven days of the feast, “sacrificing peace offerings and giving thanks (מִתְוַדִּים) to Yahweh, the God of their fathers”.

phrases.phrase: הוֹדוּ לַיהוָה כִּי־טוֹב כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ
phrases.gloss: give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his חֶסֶד is forever
give thanks to the name of Yahweh

words.gloss: thanksgiving, praise; thank offering; confession; thanksgiving choir
words.summary: 32 uses: the noun of the hiphil, the thanks itself, the peace offering brought for it, the confession of sin, and in Nehemiah the companies that sang it on the wall.

senses.definition: Thanks and praise spoken or sung to Yahweh.

evidence.note: “Enter his gates with תּוֹדָה, his courts with praise; give thanks to him.”
“Let us come before his face with תּוֹדָה; let us shout to him with psalms.”
“I will praise the name of God with a song and magnify him with תּוֹדָה; and it will please Yahweh more than an ox.”
“To make heard the voice of תּוֹדָה and tell all your wonders.”
In comforted Zion, “joy and gladness, תּוֹדָה and the voice of song”.
“Out of them shall go out תּוֹדָה and the voice of those who make merry.”
“I will sacrifice to you with the voice of תּוֹדָה.”

senses.definition: The peace offering brought for thanksgiving: with unleavened cakes and leavened bread, its flesh eaten on the day it is offered.

evidence.note: “If he offers it for תּוֹדָה, he shall offer with the זֶבַח הַתּוֹדָה unleavened cakes mixed with oil.”
With loaves of leavened bread.
Its flesh “shall be eaten on the day of its offering; he shall not leave any of it until morning”.
Israel burns leavened bread as a thank offering and boasts of it: the offering without the heart.
“Sacrifice תּוֹדָה to God and pay your vows to the Most High.”
“He who sacrifices תּוֹדָה honours me.”
“I will sacrifice to you the זֶבַח תּוֹדָה and call on the name of Yahweh.”
Those bringing תּוֹדָה into the house of Yahweh in the restored city.

senses.definition: Owning the truth to Yahweh, of sin done.

evidence.note: Joshua to Achan: “Give glory to Yahweh the God of Israel and give him תּוֹדָה; tell me now what you have done.”
“Now give תּוֹדָה to Yahweh the God of your fathers and do his will, and separate yourselves.”

senses.definition: In Nehemiah, the two great companies that went round the wall singing at its dedication.

evidence.note: “I appointed two great תּוֹדֹת and processions”, one to the right on the wall.
“So the two תּוֹדֹת stood in the house of God.”
The dedication kept “with gladness and with תּוֹדוֹת and with singing”.

evidence.locator: Lev.7.12, תּוֹדָה → αἰνέσεως (twice); Psa.116.17, תּוֹדָה → αἰνέσεως; αἴνεσις renders תּוֹדָה ×16

evidence.note: “Let us offer the θυσίαν αἰνέσεως to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name”: the Septuagint’s name for the זֶבַח תּוֹדָה, and the Peshitta’s “confessing” is מַודּיָנ of this root.

words.summary: Once, in a plural form of the hiphil’s pattern. Its sense rests on that one verse and on the other Levites of Nehemiah 12 set over thanksgiving (12:24, 27); the Septuagint read it as “hands”.

senses.definition: What Mattaniah and his brothers were set over among the Levites of the return: the songs of thanks.

evidence.note: Mattaniah, “he and his brothers, over הֻיְּדוֹת”.
The chiefs of the Levites, “to praise and to give thanks, according to the command of David”.

words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra, as the Hebrew: the hand, and power over a thing.

senses.definition: The hand itself, and in Daniel’s dream a stone cut out “not by hands”.

evidence.note: Fingers of a man’s hand wrote on the wall; the king saw the palm of the hand that wrote.
“A stone was cut out, not by hands (דִּי־לָא בִידַיִן)”, and struck the image.
The stone cut from the mountain “not by hands”: the kingdom the God of heaven sets up (2:44).

senses.definition: What is in someone’s hand is in his power or care.

evidence.note: Men, beasts and birds “he has given into your hand”.
“Who is the god who will deliver you out of my hands?”
“None can strike his hand or say to him, What are you doing?”
“The God in whose hand is your breath.”
He delivered Daniel “from the hand of the lions”.
The holy ones “shall be given into his hand for a time, times and half a time”.
The work prospers in their hands.
“According to the law of your God which is in your hand.”
Any king or people who “put out their hand” to alter the decree.

words.summary: Twice, both of Daniel, with ה or א for the Hebrew’s ה and the same w: מְהוֹדֵא, מוֹדֵא.

senses.definition: Daniel thanks God for revealing the king’s dream.

evidence.note: “To you, God of my fathers, I give thanks (מְהוֹדֵא) and praise (וּמְשַׁבַּח), for you have given me wisdom and might.”

senses.definition: Daniel’s thanks with his prayer three times a day, kept against the king’s decree.

evidence.note: Three times a day he knelt “and prayed and gave thanks (מוֹדֵא) before his God, as he had done before”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܝܕܐ (ʾīdā), about 360 times, for χείρ, including where the New Testament quotes the Hebrew יָד.

senses.definition: The hand, and the power or keeping it stands for; with a negative, what no human hand made.

evidence.note: “Father, בִּאידַֿיכּ, into your hands, I commit my spirit”: Psa 31:6.
“Has not אִידָֿא דִּילי, my hand, made all these?”: Isa 66:2.
“The heavens are the work of אִידַֿיכּ”: Psa 102:26.
“No man shall snatch them out of my hand … out of my Father’s hand”, as none delivers out of Yahweh’s (Deu 32:39).
To fall בִּאידַֿוה_י, into the hands of the living God.
A temple “made with hands” and another “not made with hands”, דּלָא עבִֿידֿ בִּאידַֿיָא.

words.gloss: (aphel) give thanks, confess, acknowledge; (eshtaphal) promise, agree
words.summary: The Peshitta’s verb, about 80 times. Its aphel ܐܘܕܝ (ʾawdī), with the same w as the Hebrew hiphil, renders both ἐξομολογέω and εὐχαριστέω and ὁμολογέω: thanks, confession of sins, and confession of Christ. Its eshtaphal ܐܫܬܘܕܝ is to promise or agree, a sense the Hebrew does not show.

senses.definition: Thank God openly, as the Hebrew hiphil.

evidence.note: דַּאודֵּא לָכֿ בּעַמ_מֵא, “I will give thanks to you among the nations”: Psa 18:50.
מַודֵּא א_נָא לָכֿ אָבֿי, “I thank you, my Father”.
Anna “gave thanks to the Lord” (וַאודּיַתֿ למָריָא).
The Samaritan fell at Jesus’ feet, מַודֵּא לֵה, giving him thanks.
“The fruit of lips דּמַודּיָנ לַשמֵה, confessing (thanking) his name.”

senses.definition: Own openly: one’s sins, and Jesus as the Christ and Lord.

evidence.note: Baptised in the Jordan, כַּדֿ מַודֵּינ בַּחטָהַיהֻונ, “confessing their sins”.
“Whoever confesses me (נַודֵּא בִּי) before men, I will confess him before my Father.”
John “confessed and did not deny, and confessed, I am not the Christ”.
“Every tongue shall confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.”
“Every tongue shall confess (נַודֵּא) to God”: Isa 45:23, whose Hebrew verb is תִּשָּׁבַע, “swear”.

senses.definition: Bind oneself by word: God’s promise to Abraham, and the priests’ agreement to pay Judas.

evidence.note: God gave Abraham no inheritance in the land, “and promised (וֵאשתַּודִּי) to give it to him and his seed”.
The time of the promise “which God had promised (דֵּאשתַּודִּי) to Abraham”.
The chief priests “promised” Judas money.
Judas “agreed” (וֵאשתַּודִּי) and sought an opportunity.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܬܘܕܝܬܐ (tawdītā), 17 times, the Syriac form of תּוֹדָה: thanksgiving (εὐχαριστία) and the confession of faith (ὁμολογία).

senses.definition: Thanks to God, offered with prayer.

evidence.note: “In prayer and petition וַבֿתַֿודִּיתָֿא, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known before God.”
How shall the unlearned say Amen at תַּודִּיתָֿכֿ, your thanksgiving?

senses.definition: What is openly owned and held: the confession of Christ and of the hope.

evidence.note: “You confessed (וַאודִּיתֿ) the good confession (תַּודִּיתָֿא) before many witnesses.”
Jesus Christ, “apostle and high priest of our תַּודִּיתָֿא”.
“Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܫܘܘܕܝܐ (šuwdāyā), 13 times, for ἐπαγγελία: the noun of the eshtaphal “promise”. The Hebrew has no word of this sense from the root.

senses.definition: What God has bound himself by word to give: the holy spirit, the inheritance promised to Abraham.

evidence.note: Wait for “the promise of the Father”.
“The promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are far off.”
“That we might receive the promise of the spirit through faith.”
God willing to show the heirs of the promise that his counsel does not change, “confirmed it by an oath”.

cognates.gloss: hand, arm; foreleg; power, authority; a benefit or favour done
cognates.note: Lane’s article gives the hand and arm, the foreleg of a beast, تَحْتَ يَدِهِ “under his authority”, عَلَى يَدِهِ “by his agency” (Lane himself compares the Hebrew), and “I owe such a one a benefit (يَدٌ)”: power, agency and possession as in the Hebrew.

evidence.note: “The arm, from the shoulder-joint to the extremities of the fingers … عَلَى يَدِهِ By his agency, or means … تَحْتَ يَدِهِ Under his authority … I owe such a one a benefit.”

cognates.gloss: arm; side; strength, power; wages, hire
cognates.note: Akkadian’s everyday word for “hand” is qātu; idu is the arm, and like the Hebrew יָד also the side of a thing and strength.

evidence.note: arm; direction; handle; power; side; strength; wages

cognates.gloss: hand; portion; (byd) from the hand of, because of; (preposition) with
cognates.note: The Ugaritic hand also means a portion, as the Hebrew יָדוֹת “shares” (Gen 43:34), and byd “from the hand of” is the Hebrew מִיַּד.

evidence.note: “hand” … 1.14:III:13 “portion”; ydk 1.23:47 “(member >) penis”; byd 3.4:14 “from (the hand of)”; 1.6:II:25 “because of”; also yd preposition “(together) with”.
“hand”; from Proto-Semitic *yad-.

cognates.note: Kilamuwa’s “each extended his hand to fight” and “in the hand of those kings I was like a fire”; and “in him was the strength (yd) of Baal”.

evidence.note: “n.f. 1. HAND, ARM … 2. STRENGTH”; KAI 24.5–6, KAI 30.2.

cognates.gloss: hand, arm; leg (of animals); part; side

evidence.note: “hand, arm, leg (of animals), part, side”.

cognates.gloss: hand; (עַל יְדֵי) through, by means of
cognates.note: The Targums’ hand, with עַל יְדֵי “through” (an agent) as Hebrew בְּיַד.

evidence.note: Targ. Num. XXXV, 17; Targ. Is. XIII, 7; עַל יְדֵי Targ. Ps. LXXXIX, 20; Targ. Y. Num. XXXIII, 1.

cognates.note: The first letter is w: the verb “throw” is *wdy, as the Hebrew hiphil הוֹדָה and hithpael הִתְוַדָּה also show, and not the y of the hand.

evidence.note: “to cast, throw, put on”; compare Hebrew יָדָה.

cognates.note: One word, read either way: the root list sets it under *wdy “throw”, Segert’s glossary under “scratch” (in mourning, 1.5 VI 18), so it does not settle the sense.

cognates.note: The Targums split the root as the Hebrew does: the causative is to admit or give thanks, the reflexive to confess sin (Onkelos Lev 5:5, for the Hebrew hithpael), each with the w. The Peshitta’s ʾawdī, “give thanks, confess”, is the same.

evidence.note: Pa. וַדֵּי, Ithpa. אִתְוַדֵּי “to confess”, Targ. O. Lev. V, 5; Af. אוֹדִי, הוֹדִי, Targ. Prov. XXVIII, 13; Targ. Gen. XLIX, 8; “he must offer thanks”.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh’s hand is his power at work. With “a strong hand and an outstretched arm” he brought Israel out of Egypt (Deu 26:8); his hand is not too short to save (Num 11:23; Isa 59:1); his hand made heaven and earth (Isa 66:2, quoted in Act 7:50; Psa 102:26, quoted in Heb 1:10). When it is “on” a prophet he is moved by it to see and to speak: “the hand of Yahweh was on me, and he brought me out by the spirit of Yahweh” (Ezk 37:1; also 1:3; 3:14; 2Ki 3:15). Jesus’ words “if I by the finger of God cast out demons” (Luk 11:20) are in Matthew “by the spirit of God” (Mat 12:28). From the verses: hand, finger and spirit are scripture’s names for one thing, God’s own power put forth, and not for a person beside him.

The verb that thanks Yahweh for his goodness also confesses sin: both are owning openly what is true, of him and of oneself. The law required the guilty man to confess the sin he had done with his offering or restitution (Lev 5:5; Num 5:7); the high priest confessed all Israel’s iniquities over the living goat (Lev 16:21); and Yahweh promised that if Israel in exile confessed their iniquity he would remember his covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham (Lev 26:40–42). David: “My iniquity I did not cover; I said, I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh, and you forgave” (Psa 32:5); “he who covers his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will find mercy” (Pro 28:13). Daniel, Ezra and Nehemiah confessed the nation’s sins (Dan 9:4, 20; Ezr 10:1; Neh 9:2). Those John baptised came “confessing their sins” (Mat 3:6; Mrk 1:5), and “if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins” (1Jn 1:9). From the verses: forgiveness is promised to sin owned and forsaken, not to sin covered.

Thanksgiving belongs to the living. Hezekiah, raised from his sickness: “The grave does not thank you, death does not praise you; those who go down to the pit do not hope for your faithfulness. The living, the living, he thanks you, as I do this day” (Isa 38:18–19). “In death there is no remembrance of you; in the grave who will thank you?” (Psa 6:6). “Will the dust thank you? Will it declare your faithfulness?” (Psa 30:10). “Will you work wonders for the dead? Will the shades rise and thank you?” (Psa 88:11). The preacher says the same without the verb: “the dead know nothing … there is no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in the grave” (Ecc 9:5, 10). From the verses: the dead are not alive elsewhere giving thanks; they lie silent in the grave, and the only way they will thank God again is the one Psalm 88 asks about, rising from it (Isa 26:19; Dan 12:2).

The thank offering (זֶבַח תּוֹדָה) was a peace offering brought for thanks, with unleavened cakes and leavened bread, its flesh eaten the day it was offered (Lev 7:12–15; 22:29–30). The psalms make the thanks itself the offering God asks for: “Sacrifice thanksgiving to God and pay your vows to the Most High” (Psa 50:14); “he who sacrifices thanksgiving honours me” (Psa 50:23); a song with thanksgiving “will please Yahweh more than an ox” (Psa 69:31–32); and Jeremiah foresees thank offerings and the cry “give thanks to Yahweh of hosts, for Yahweh is good” in Jerusalem again (Jer 33:11). Hebrews: “Through him let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name” (Heb 13:15), where θυσία αἰνέσεως is the Septuagint’s name for the זֶבַח תּוֹדָה (Lev 7:12) and the Peshitta’s “confessing” is the verb of this root. From the verses: the animal offerings end in Christ’s own, but the thank offering goes on, as thanks spoken to God through him.

Nebuchadnezzar saw a stone “cut out not by hands” (Aramaic דִּי־לָא בִידַיִן) strike the image on its feet and become a mountain filling the whole earth; Daniel explains it as the kingdom the God of heaven will set up, which will break all these kingdoms and stand forever (Dan 2:34–35, 44–45). What men’s hands make, God does not need: “Has not my hand made all these things?” (Isa 66:2, quoted in Act 7:48–50). The New Testament keeps the contrast: the temple “not made with hands” Jesus would raise (Mrk 14:58), the greater tabernacle “not made with hands” and the holy place “not made with hands” Christ entered (Heb 9:11, 24), the circumcision “made without hands” (Col 2:11), the house “not made with hands, eternal in the heavens” (2Co 5:1). From the verses: the kingdom of Daniel 2 is God’s own work, not built by men, and it comes when Christ returns and breaks the kingdoms of men, as the stone strikes the image.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה, Num 10:13; the name Judah, 10:14); neither word occurs in Leviticus 23. Root keys: the corpus files the hand j.aq.aa with no root and the Aramaic hand xj.aa.ad under יד, and the verb and its nouns under ידה; the entry takes ידה as its root at the task’s direction, and יָד, which has no root key, sits under it as אָב does under אבה. The Aramaic key xj.aa.ad is double-filed on about 340 Hebrew construct tokens of בְּיַד/יַד (Gen 27:17, Num 10:13 …), so its count is far above the Aramaic’s 17 uses (Dan 2:34, 38, 45; 3:15, 17; 4:32; 5:5, 23, 24; 6:28; 7:25; Ezr 5:8, 12; 6:12; 7:14, 25). Two roots? The hand is *yad with an original y in every language (Arabic yad, Akkadian idu, Ge'ez ʾəd); the verb shows w in the Hebrew hiphil and hithpael (הוֹדָה, הִתְוַדָּה, as הוֹשִׁיב from *wṯb), in Biblical Aramaic מְהוֹדֵא, Targum אוֹדִי/אִתְוַדֵּי, Syriac ʾawdī, and Ge'ez wadaya “throw”. So the evidence points to *wdy for the verb and *yd for the noun: one spelling, two older roots, which the Sounds scheme (ח ע ש ז צ only) cannot record. Whether “throw” and “give thanks / confess” are one root is not shown either (Ge'ez “throw”, Aramaic and Syriac only “thank, confess”). Left out: the zero-token cross-references e.ay.ag, e.be.ae, j.at.ah, j.at.aj, w.ah.ak; the names Jeduthun (j.at.ae), Hodaviah (j.at.ab), Jedaiah (j.at.af), and Jidlaph (j.at.ak, whose link to this root is BDB’s filing only), which belong in names/; Judah has its own name entry (names/judah.json); the place יִדְאֲלָה (j.aq.ab). Klein’s noun יָדָה “cuff” is post-biblical. Not consulted: Payne Smith for the Syriac (SEDRA used), Dillmann and Leslau for Ge'ez (Wiktionary and the root list only), DULAT for Ugaritic ydy. Arabic يَدَى “do good to” (Wiktionary) and Lane’s يَدٌ “benefit” were not followed further as a bridge to “thank”. Open questions: (1) keep the hand and the verb together, or split to an entry under יד; (2) the Syriac eshtaphal “promise” and its noun, with no Hebrew counterpart; (3) the doctrine notes on the hand of Yahweh and the spirit, and on Daniel 2. Peshitta words: SEDRA root 58 ܝܕ, lexeme 74 ܐܝܕܐ; root 767 ܝܕܐ, lexemes 1298 (verb), 1299 ܫܘܘܕܝܐ, 1300 ܬܘܕܝܬܐ; their verses found through the Peshitta text, glosses from SEDRA.
